origin.description: Sen index of poverty for an income vector at an absolute poverty line.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Income vector. The index is defined for non-negative values.

arguments.name: k
arguments.text: Absolute poverty line, a single constant.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values before computing. If false, any missing value makes the result missing.

origin.details: The index is the headcount times a mix of the average shortfall and inequality among people strictly below the line. That inequality is the Gini coefficient of those incomes. When nobody is strictly below the line, the index is 0.
origin.value: A single number, the Sen index.
origin.example:
# generate vectors (of incomes)
x <- c(541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261)
y <- c(841, 2063, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11304, 21961)
# compute Watts index with poverty line 2000
pov(x, 2000)
pov(y, 2000)
# compute headcount ratio with poverty line 2000
pov(x, 2000, parameter=1, type="Foster")
pov(y, 2000, parameter=1, type="Foster")

translation.description: Sen index of poverty for an income vector at an absolute poverty line.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Income vector. The index is defined for non-negative values. Missing values are NaN.

arguments.name: k
arguments.text: Absolute poverty line, a single constant.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values before computing. If false, any missing value makes the result NaN.

translation.details: The index is H * (I + (1 - I) * G). H is the share of the sample strictly below the line, I is the average shortfall of those incomes as a fraction of the line, and G is Gini on that same subset. When nobody is strictly below the line, the index is 0.
translation.value: A single number, the Sen index.
translation.example:
from ineq.poverty import pov

# generate vectors (of incomes)
x = [541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261]
y = [841, 2063, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11304, 21961]
# compute Watts index with poverty line 2000
print(pov(x, 2000))
print(pov(y, 2000))
# compute headcount ratio with poverty line 2000
print(pov(x, 2000, parameter=1, type="Foster"))
print(pov(y, 2000, parameter=1, type="Foster"))
